summary.intent: Continue a GSD (multi-phase planning/execution framework) session on cipher-box: verify Phase 69, plan Phase 70 and discuss Phase 71, then execute Phase 70's 8 plans across 6 waves.
summary.outcome: Phase 69 marked complete (already-shipped), Phase 70 fully planned (8 plans/6 waves, checker passed) and execution began — branch name mismatch was reconciled and Wave 1 (plan 70-01, a local-wins 3-way merge in rotation/merge.ts) was dispatched via a gsd-executor subagent; Phase 71 requirements were locked into a context doc but not yet planned.

repo: gsd-execute-phase's `handle_branching` init computes an expected branch name via truncation that can diverge from the actual branch name a prior plan-phase run created (e.g. plan-created `feat/rotation-soundness-deep-merge-fresh-record-resume` vs execute-phase's computed `...-and-durabl`); if left alone it forks a new branch off origin/main missing all planned commits — fix by renaming the existing branch to match the expected name rather than letting init fork fresh.

The gsd-execute-phase worktree-isolated executor/merge machinery carries real corruption risk — the workflow's own docs reference a past incident of a wrong-base merge that nearly shipped ~1000 files — so for phases where only one wave can actually parallelize, sequential execution on the main tree (still via gsd-executor subagents, just one at a time) is safer than paying the worktree merge/cleanup risk.

Phase 70's wave graph: Wave 1 has 3 independent plans (70-01 sdk-core merge, 70-02 Rust floor store, 70-03 web driver) with zero file overlap; Waves 2-6 are single-plan each and all serialize because they touch engine.ts.
workflow: In top-level Claude Code (Agent tool available), gsd-execute-phase must dispatch work as gsd-executor subagents rather than executing inline — inline execution is only authorized in runtimes without an Agent tool (e.g. plain Copilot chat).

friction: Branch-name computation mismatch between the phase-70 planning run and execute-phase's init step required manual reconciliation before execution could proceed safely.
